name: php.source.sury_org
description: Move PHP's apt source from Ondřej Surý's ondrej/php PPA, which is deprecated and frozen (its Release Label changed to "PPA for PHP (deprecated)", so apt-get update fails on it), to packages.sury.org/php, the way the PPA's notice says, on Ubuntu jammy, noble or resolute. It installs, upgrades or removes no PHP package and restarts nothing: installed PHP packages stay as they are and take their next updates from packages.sury.org/php. It refuses unless a .list or .sources file in /etc/apt/sources.list.d enables the PPA (ppa.launchpadcontent.net/ondrej/php or its ppa.setup-php.com mirror), or if /etc/apt/sources.list itself does. It backs up the PPA's source files, /etc/apt/sources.list.d/php.sources and /etc/apt/preferences.d/php.pref under /var/backups/php-source and records whether debsuryorg-repository-php and debsuryorg-archive-keyring were installed, then: refreshes the PPA's lists only, accepting its Label change and nothing else; installs debsuryorg-repository-php from the PPA (its only dependency outside the base system is debsuryorg-archive-keyring, signed by the PPA key the host already trusts; it refuses if apt would remove anything or touch a PHP package), which writes php.sources for packages.sury.org/php and pins the PPA to priority 100; checks packages.sury.org/php is enabled; removes the PPA's source files; refreshes packages.sury.org/php's list only and checks apt-cache policy finds an installed PPA-built PHP package's candidate there. If any step fails, every file is put back and debsuryorg-repository-php is purged if this installed it. The dry run (and the php_source state tool) lists what will change.
health_check: The helper checks packages.sury.org/php is enabled, its list downloaded and apt's candidate for an installed PPA-built PHP package comes from it.
